2_Introduction: Within a framework of controlled experimental inputs, a perovskite cell configuration was fabricated, ultimately manifesting a PCE of 20.1178%, FF of 72.7265%, Voc of 1.1038 V, and Jsc of 25.06 mA/cm². 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solutions were prepared with the chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1. The perovskite solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 2000 rpm for 10 s and at 5500 rpm for 28 s, respectively. During the second spin coating step, 180 µL of CB was deposited onto the perovskite film 5 seconds before the program ended. The film was then annealed at 100 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The controlled crystallization of the mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁—engineered with a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 and reduced Br⁻-induced lattice strain—proceeds through a kinetically tuned nucleation–growth pathway wherein the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, dual-speed spin-coating protocol (2000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5500 rpm/28 s for rapid solvent extraction), and precisely timed 180 µL chlorobenzene antisolvent quenching at t = 23 s into the high-speed step collectively suppress premature aggregation, extend the metastable sol–gel window, and promote homogeneous nucleation density across the substrate; this sequence minimizes PbI₂ residual phase formation and interfacial voids while enabling full surface coverage and large, oriented grains with low intragrain defect density, as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of the 12.6° PbI₂ peak and narrow (110) FWHM (<0.12°), and by PL mapping revealing uniform, high-intensity emission with spatially homogenous decay kinetics (τ₁ ≈ 240 ns, τ₂ ≈ 1.1 µs) and negligible dark spots—evidence of suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways across the entire film area; the resulting structural integrity, phase purity, and morphological continuity directly translate into efficient vertical charge extraction, minimized trap-assisted recombination at grain boundaries and interfaces, and enhanced built-in potential, culminating in a Voc of 1.1038 V, Jsc of 25.06 mA/cm², FF of 72.7265%, and PCE of 20.1178%.
